items.name: General concepts:
items.group: 3. Web APIs › 3.1 Video and audio APIs
parts: Understand the different types of video and audio formats.
Understand codecs.
Understand key functionality associated with audio and video — play, pause, stop, seeking backward and forward, duration, and current time.
items.note: مفيش درس JS عن play/pause/seeking/duration/currentTime؛ الـ formats والـ codecs في css tab «audio و source» و«video و iframe» بس كـ HTML

items.name: Using the HTMLMediaElement API to build a basic custom media player:
items.group: 3. Web APIs › 3.1 Video and audio APIs
parts: Understand why you'd do this — your target audience might have specific needs not addressed by the browser defaults.
One good example is that some browser default controls are not very keyboard accessible.
Another is that you might just want a consistent UI design across browsers.
items.note: مفيش درس بيبني media player مخصص بـ HTMLMediaElement ولا بيشرح ليه (accessibility، شكل موحد)

items.name: Using media streams/getUserMedia() to capture video and audio from a local device.
items.group: 3. Web APIs › 3.1 Video and audio APIs
items.note: مفيش درس getUserMedia / MediaStream

items.name: Handling common errors related to media delivery:
items.group: 3. Web APIs › 3.1 Video and audio APIs
parts: Using <source> elements to handle multiple formats.
Using the correct MIME type.
Showing fallback content if the media is not supported.
items.note: الـ source والـ MIME type والـ fallback متشرحين في css tab «audio و source»، مش في js

items.name: Understand the purpose of other video and audio APIs, including the Web Audio API, Media Stream Recording API, and Media Source Extensions API.
items.group: 3. Web APIs › 3.1 Video and audio APIs
items.note: مفيش درس لـ Web Audio و MediaRecorder و Media Source Extensions

items.name: Using timers and requestAnimationFrame() to set up animation loops:
parts: Basic syntax and usage.
Understand why requestAnimationFrame() is an improvement over what came before it.
Common use cases for animation loops, for example, decorative animations and games.

items.name: Web Animations API:
parts: Basic syntax and usage.
Understand how the Web Animations API relates to CSS animation properties, and when should you use each one.
Common use cases.
items.note: مفيش درس لـ Web Animations API (element.animate) ولا الفرق بينها وبين CSS animations

items.name: Canvas:
parts: Understand conceptually what the <canvas> element and associated APIs enable.
Basic syntax and usage of the 2D Canvas API.
Looping <canvas> updates to create a simple animation or game.

items.name: Understand the concepts of client-side storage:
parts: Know the common client-side data storage mechanisms — Web Storage API, cookies, Cache API, and the IndexedDB API.
Key use cases — maintaining state across reloads, persisting login and user personalization data, and local/offline working.
Understand the negative patterns associated with client-side storage — for example using cookies for tracking/fingerprinting.
items.note: مفيش درس مقارنة بين cookies و Web Storage و Cache و IndexedDB ولا مخاطر الـ tracking/fingerprinting؛ web tab «localStorage و JWT» بيغطي جزء

items.name: Using cookies to store arbitrary data, normally controlled by HTTP headers.
items.note: الكوكيز (Set-Cookie, HttpOnly, SameSite) ظاهرة جوه «مشروع — CORS والكوكيز» بس، مفيش درس بيشرح document.cookie وخصايصها

items.name: Using Web Storage for simple key-value pair storage, controlled by JavaScript.
Using IndexedDB:
parts: Complete client-side transactional database system.
Complex, and rarely used directly. You'd be more likely to use a library such as dexie.js.

items.name: Using Cache/Service Workers:
parts: Understand the basic ideas behind their usage in Progressive Web Apps (PWAs), and the fundamental use case of making a site work offline.

items.name: Understand what variables are and why they are so important in programming generally, not just JavaScript.
Declaring variables with let and initializing them with values.
The difference between variables and constants, and when you would use each one.
Understand variable naming best practices. If not explicitly covered, all examples should show good variable naming pratices in action.
The different types of value that can be stored in variables — strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects.
Basic number operations in JavaScript — add, subtract, multiply, and divide.
Understand that numbers are not numbers if they are defined as strings, and how this can cause calculations to go wrong.
Converting strings to numbers with Number().
items.at: number و NaN › تحويل نص لرقم

items.name: Incrementing and decrementing.
items.at: ++ و -- و += وأخواتها › ١. الزيادة والنقص بواحد

items.name: Assignment operators, e.g. addition assignment and subtraction assignment.
Basic Math object methods, such as Math.random(), Math.floor(), and Math.ceil().
Understand the need for matching quotes.
items.at: string literals و String() › ٢. لازم العلامتين يبقوا شبه بعض

items.name: Escaping characters in strings.
items.at: escape sequences و String.raw › ١. escape يعني إيه

items.name: Template literals:
parts: Using variables in template literals.
Multiline template literals.

items.name: String manipulation using common properties and methods such as:
parts: length.
toString().
includes().
indexOf().
slice().
toLowerCase() and toUpperCase().
replace().
items.at: string: indexOf و substring و concat › ١. String.prototype.indexOf

items.name: Understand what an array is — a structure that holds a list of variables.
items.note: مفيش درس مقدمة للـ arrays (يعني إيه array وليه)

items.name: The syntax of arrays — [a, b, c] and the accessor syntax, myArray[x].
items.note: مفيش درس مقدمة للـ arrays: syntax والـ index و arr[0] مفترضين معروفين

items.name: Modifying array values with myArray[x] = y.
items.note: مفيش درس بيشرح arr[i] = value (تعديل عنصر بالـ index)

items.name: Array manipulation using common properties and methods, such as:
parts: length.
indexOf().
push() and pop().
shift() and unshift().
join() and split().
items.note: مفيش درس array methods الأساسية: pop و shift و length مش متشرحين، وpush/join/unshift/indexOf/split متفرقين في تمارين ودروس تانية

items.name: Advanced array methods such as forEach(), map() and filter().
Understand what a conditional is — a code structure for running different code paths depending on a test result.
Using comparison operators to create tests.
AND, OR, and NOT in tests.
Ternary operators.
items.at: if و else if › الـ ternary

items.name: Understand the purpose of loops — a code structure that allows you to do something very similar many times without repeating the same code for each iteration.
Basic for loops.
items.at: for و while › عدد لفات معروف

items.name: Looping through collections with for ... of.
Understand the purpose of functions — to enable the creation of reusable blocks of code that can be called wherever needed.
Understand that functions are used everywhere in JavaScript and that some are built into the browser and some are user-defined.
items.note: مفيش شرح صريح إن فيه دوال مدمجة (console.log و Math.*) ودوال بتكتبها انت

items.name: Understand the difference between functions and methods.
Understand global scope and function/block scope.
Passing in arguments to function calls.
Building your own custom functions:
parts: Including parameters.
Including return values.

items.name: Callback functions — understand that arguments to functions can themselves be functions, and what this pattern is used for.
Arrow functions.
items.at: function و arrow › arrow function بسطر واحد

items.name: Understand that in JavaScript most things are objects, and you've probably used objects every time you've touched JavaScript.
Basic syntax:
parts: Object literals.
Properties and methods.
Nesting objects and arrays in objects.

items.name: Using constructors to create a new object.
Accessing properties and methods — bracket and dot syntax.
Understand what the DOM is — the browser's internal representation of the document's HTML structure as a hierarchy of objects, which can be manipulated using JavaScript.
Understand the important parts of a web browser and how they are represented in JavaScript — Navigator, Window, and Document.
items.note: مفيش درس بيشرح Window و Navigator و Document كأجزاء المتصفح (navigator بتظهر في Clipboard بس)

items.name: Understand how DOM nodes exist relative to each other in the DOM tree — root, parent, child, sibling, and descendant.
items.note: مفيش درس بيشرح علاقات العقد في الشجرة (parent/child/sibling و parentElement و nextElementSibling و children)

items.name: Getting references to DOM nodes, for example with querySelector() and getElementById().
Creating new nodes, for example with innerHTML() and createElement().
Adding and removing nodes to the DOM with appendChild() and removeChild().
Manipulating styles with Element.style.* and Element.classList.*.
Understand what events are — a signal fired by the browser when something significant happens, which the developer can run some code in response to.
Event handlers:
parts: addEventListener() and removeEventListener()
Event handler properties.
Inline event handler attributes, and why you shouldn't use them.
items.note: addEventListener/removeEventListener متشرحين، لكن event handler properties (el.onclick =) والـ inline attributes (onclick="") وليه نتجنبها مش متشرحين

items.name: Understand the concept of asynchronous JavaScript — what it is and how it differs from synchronous JavaScript.
Understand that callbacks and events have historically provided the means to do asynchronous programming in JavaScript.
items.note: مفيش شرح لتاريخ الـ callbacks والـ events كأساس الـ async قبل Promises؛ callback hell مذكورة مرة في Promise

items.name: Modern asynchronous programming with async functions and await:
parts: Basic usage.
Understanding async function return values.
Error handling with try ... catch.

items.name: Promises:
parts: Understand that async/await use promises under the hood; they provide a simpler abstraction.
Chaining promises.
Catching errors with catch().

items.name: Understand that fetch() is used for asynchronous network requests, which is by far the most common asynchronous JavaScript use case on the web.
items.group: 6. JavaScript fundamentals › 6.12 Network requests with fetch()

items.name: Common types of resources that are fetched from the network:
items.group: 6. JavaScript fundamentals › 6.12 Network requests with fetch()
parts: Text content, JSON, media assets, etc.
Data from RESTful APIs. Learn the basic concepts behind REST, including common patterns such as CRUD.
items.note: fetch للـ JSON متغطي، لكن مفيش درس بيشرح REST و CRUD كمفاهيم، ولا fetch لـ text/media

items.name: Understand what single-page apps (SPAs) are, and the issues surrounding them:
items.group: 6. JavaScript fundamentals › 6.12 Network requests with fetch()
parts: Accessibility issues behind asynchronous updates, for example, content updates not being announced by screen readers by default.
Usability issues behind asynchronous updates, like loss of history and breaking the back button.

items.name: Understand HTTP basics. You should look at common HTTP methods such as GET, DELETE, POST, and PUT, and how they are handled via fetch().

items.name: Why developers use third-party code:
parts: Efficiency and productivity: A huge amount of complex functionality is already written for you to use, created in a way that enforces efficient, modular code organization.

Compatibility: Reputable framework code is already optimized to work across browsers/devices, for performance, etc. Many frameworks also have systems to output to specific platforms (e.g. Android or iOS) as build targets.
Support/ecosystem: Popular frameworks have vibrant communities and help resources to provide support, and rich systems of extensions/plugins to add functionality.

items.name: The difference between libraries and frameworks:
parts: A library tends to be a single code component that offers a solution to a specific problem, which you can integrate into your own app (for example, chart.js for creating <canvas>-based charts, or three.js for simplified 3D GPU-based graphics rendering), whereas a framework tends to be a more expansive architecture made up of multiple components for building complete applications.
A library tends to be unopinionated about how you work with it in your codebase, whereas a framework tends to enforce a specific coding style and control flow.

items.name: Why should you use frameworks?
parts: They can provide a lot of functionality and save you a lot of time.
A lot of companies use popular frameworks such as React or Angular to write their applications, therefore a lot of jobs list frameworks as requirements for applicants to have.

items.name: Why is a framework not always the right choice? A framework:
parts: Can easily be overkill for a small project — you might be better off writing a few lines of vanilla JavaScript to solve the problem or using a tailored library.
Usually adds a lot of JavaScript to the initial download of your application, leading to an initial performance hit and possible usability issues.
Usually comes with its own set of custom syntax and conventions, which can introduce a significant additional learning curve to the project.
May be incompatible with an existing codebase because of its architecture choice.
Will need to be updated regularly, possibly leading to extra maintenance overhead for your application.

May introduce significant accessibility issues for people using assistive technologies because of its architecture (for example, SPA-style client-side routing), which will need to be considered carefully.

items.name: How to choose? A good library or framework must:
parts: Solve your problems while offering advantages that significantly outweigh any negatives that it brings to the table.
Have good support and a friendly community.
Be actively maintained — don't choose a codebase that has not been updated for over a year, or has no users.
